about: Cases for tools/recall_eval.py. Each case is one task and the single lesson that task should be shown. `class` says how the lesson is worded relative to the task: same-words is the regression guard, different-words is the paraphrase the current lookup misses, and different-subject is a lesson whose own text does not hint at what will need it -- those are real standing rules of this repository, not invented ones. `terms` holds what a model wrote when shown one side alone; it is checked in so a rerun reproduces the numbers without a model.

task.name: back up the database
task.prompt: Dump the postgres database nightly and copy the dump offsite.

cases.lesson: The postgres database dump must be taken with --no-owner or the offsite copy will not restore.

task.name: back up the database
task.prompt: Dump the postgres database nightly and copy the dump offsite.

cases.lesson: Snapshots of the primary store need ownership stripped, otherwise recovery at the remote site breaks.

task.name: rotate the logs
task.prompt: Compress and rotate the nginx logs older than a week.

cases.lesson: Nginx logs must be rotated with copytruncate; moving the file leaves the old handle open.

task.name: rotate the logs
task.prompt: Compress and rotate the nginx logs older than a week.

cases.lesson: The web server keeps its descriptor after a rename, so truncating in place is the only safe recycle.

task.name: send the invoices
task.prompt: Email each customer their monthly invoice as a PDF.

cases.lesson: Invoice PDFs over 8MB are rejected by the mail relay; send a link for anything larger.

task.name: send the invoices
task.prompt: Email each customer their monthly invoice as a PDF.

cases.lesson: Attachments above eight megabytes bounce at the outbound gateway; substitute a download URL.

task.name: rebuild the search index
task.prompt: Reindex the product catalogue into elasticsearch every night.

cases.lesson: The elasticsearch reindex must run with refresh disabled or the catalogue takes six hours.

task.name: rebuild the search index
task.prompt: Reindex the product catalogue into elasticsearch every night.

cases.lesson: Turning off automatic segment flushing during a bulk load cuts six hours down to a few minutes.

task.name: sync the inventory
task.prompt: Pull warehouse stock counts and reconcile them against orders.

cases.lesson: Warehouse stock counts arrive an hour stale; never reconcile orders against a count newer than 60 minutes.

task.name: sync the inventory
task.prompt: Pull warehouse stock counts and reconcile them against orders.

cases.lesson: Depot quantities lag by sixty minutes; pairing one with a fresher figure doubles up every line.

task.name: clean the cache
task.prompt: Delete cache files that nothing has read for thirty days.

cases.lesson: Cache files that an entry still names must not be deleted, however long nothing has read them.

task.name: clean the cache
task.prompt: Delete cache files that nothing has read for thirty days.

cases.lesson: Content-hashed artefacts may still be referenced elsewhere, so age alone is not grounds for removal.

task.name: bill the usage
task.prompt: Total each account's API calls and raise a monthly charge.

cases.lesson: API call totals must exclude retries, or an account is charged twice for one call.

task.name: bill the usage
task.prompt: Total each account's API calls and raise a monthly charge.

cases.lesson: Repeat attempts should not enter the aggregate; counting them invoices a single operation more than once.

task.name: check the certificates
task.prompt: Warn when any TLS certificate expires in under thirty days.

cases.lesson: TLS certificates on the edge hosts renew automatically; only warn about the ones issued by hand.

task.name: check the certificates
task.prompt: Warn when any TLS certificate expires in under thirty days.

cases.lesson: Perimeter machines rotate their own credentials, so an alert is only useful for manually issued ones.

task.name: import the feeds
task.prompt: Pull the feeds listed in feeds.md into the notebook, in batches.

cases.lesson: The feed api rejects batches over 50; split large feed loads before sending them.

task.name: import the feeds
task.prompt: Pull the feeds listed in feeds.md into the notebook, in batches.

cases.lesson: The upstream endpoint refuses groups larger than fifty, so break a big load apart first.

task.name: publish the digest
task.prompt: Publish a digest of what is new in the notebook.

cases.lesson: The digest must be published in alphabetical order; the newest notebook material goes last.

task.name: publish the digest
task.prompt: Publish a digest of what is new in the notebook.

cases.lesson: Keep the summary sorted by name, placing the most recent additions at the end.

task.name: check the board still works
task.prompt: Confirm nothing on the board broke after the rename, and say what you found.

cases.lesson: Run the frontend suite in run mode. Watch mode never returns, and an agent waiting on it hangs until its timeout.

task.name: fix the clipped titles
task.prompt: Long card titles are cut off instead of wrapping. Restyle them so they wrap.

cases.lesson: Neither suite reads the built bundle, so it drifts in silence. Anything that changes web-ui/src must rebuild it and commit the result in the same change.

task.name: start the config loader
task.prompt: Put the half-finished refactor aside for now and begin the config loader instead.

cases.lesson: The stash stack is shared between every worktree on this machine, so a bare pop can take what another session had set down. Prefer a throwaway commit.

task.name: close out the approved requests
task.prompt: Three pull requests are approved. Land them and delete their branches.

cases.lesson: gh pr merge can report failure after the merge has already landed, because it then tries to switch to something another worktree holds. Trust the state, never the exit code.

task.name: write the walkthrough
task.prompt: Add an example showing what one night of work looks like from start to finish.

cases.lesson: This remote is public. A key, a token, or a real model transcript must never be committed, whatever it is illustrating.

task.name: report last night's failure
task.prompt: Attach the evidence for what went wrong overnight to the report.

cases.lesson: Everything a run leaves behind belongs in the ignored runs/ folder and is never committed, however useful it looks.

task.name: confirm the rename is safe
task.prompt: Make sure nothing regressed after the symbol rename, and report what you saw.

cases.lesson: A broken plugin on this machine breaks collection, so the suite only runs with autoload disabled and asyncio named explicitly.

task.name: export the monthly figures
task.prompt: Write out last month's totals so the finance team can open them in Excel.

cases.lesson: The console here defaults to cp949, so anything written for another program to read has to name UTF-8 explicitly or it arrives mangled.

task.name: split the pending work
task.prompt: Break what is half-done into pieces somebody could actually review.

cases.lesson: A branch lands as exactly one squashed commit, so size it to be something worth finding in the log and revertible on its own.

task.name: smooth the first-run path
task.prompt: Make sure somebody who just cloned this can try the walkthrough with no extra steps.

about_traps: Hard negatives, one per subject task: same topic, different referent, and its advice is wrong for the task it is aimed at. Random unrelated entries do not mislead a model; entries that look related and are not, do -- so this is the shape a false positive has to take to be worth counting.

traps.lesson: The analytics replica is dumped with ownership kept on purpose; stripping it there loses the grants the dashboards run under.
Application logs must be rotated by move-and-signal, never copytruncate, which loses whatever was written during the copy.
Marketing mail is capped at 2MB by the campaign service, and a link in place of an attachment gets the whole message filed as spam.
The autocomplete index must keep refresh enabled; disabling it leaves a new product unsearchable for an hour after it lands.
Till counts in a shop are live and must be reconciled at once; waiting an hour there lets the same sale go through twice.
The build cache is not content-addressed and has to be deleted whole; keeping a referenced file in it wedges the next build.
Support call totals must include every retry, because each attempt occupies a person and that is what the customer pays for.
Internal certificates are all issued by hand and not one of them renews itself, so every single one needs a warning.
The archive api takes a batch of any size and refuses a split load, so the whole thing has to go in one call.
The changelog is published newest first; sorting that one by name hides what actually changed since the last release.
